row.evidence: Notion's pricing page lists 'User provisioning (SCIM)' under Enterprise (Custom pricing, Contact Sales): 'Access the Notion SCIM API to provision and manage users and groups.' The SCIM help doc says the feature is only available on the Enterprise Plan.
row.notes: Unchanged from June: SCIM Enterprise-only (Contact Sales); Plus $10 and Business $20 per member/mo billed yearly (pricing page defaults to yearly). SAML SSO starts at Business. SCIM DELETE (or active=false) removes the member from the workspace and logs them out of all sessions; the Notion account itself is not deleted. SCIM tokens are per workspace and tied to the owner who created them (revoked if that owner leaves or is downgraded). Guests can't be managed over SCIM; profile updates need a verified email domain. Google's integration does not provision groups. New since June: an Enterprise-only Admin API (api.notion.com/admin) covers listing users, permission groups and memberships and revoking managed users' sessions, but not creating or removing members. The public API (all plans) only lists and retrieves users. Audit log is Enterprise, viewed in-app or streamed to a SIEM via webhook.

plans.name: Business
plans.notes: One SAML configuration per Business workspace.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Audit log (in-app) and SIEM streaming on Enterprise; no REST audit-log endpoint found.

scim.notes: Notion's IdP guide gives the tenant URL as https://app.notion.com/scim/v2 (see conflicts). The IdP must support SAML 2.0, but the OneLogin guide says to configure SCIM before SSO, so SSO need not be enabled first.

auth.token_source: Manage organization > General > SCIM provisioning (one token per workspace; organization owners only)
auth.token_expiry: Revoked when the creating workspace owner leaves or is downgraded; otherwise no stated expiry

deprovision.data_retained: The user is removed from the workspace but the Notion user account is not deleted (manual deletion only). Removed seats stay usable by another member until the billing period ends.

custom.how: Notion extension schema urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:notion:2.0:User with a 'role' attribute (owner | membership_admin | member | restricted_member)

roles.how: Workspace role via the Notion extension 'role' attribute (owner, membership_admin, member, restricted_member); OneLogin rules can map roles to Notion permission groups.

limitations.text: Workspace guests cannot be managed via SCIM.
Profile (name/email) updates require verified ownership of the user's email domain.
The workspace owner who created the SCIM token cannot be removed via SCIM; removing an owner revokes their tokens and breaks integrations.
Profile photo is read only at user creation; meta.created and meta.lastModified are not meaningful; only one phone number is stored.
Group deletion is refused if it would leave pages with no full-access user.
Google Workspace's SCIM integration does not provision or deprovision groups.
Deleting the Notion app in Okta removes all provisioned users from the workspace.
A separate SCIM token is needed for each workspace.

user_api.notes: Admin API (Enterprise only, organization bot token). The user and permission-group scopes are only for 'eligible' Enterprise organizations. The public Notion API (https://api.notion.com, all plans) only lists and retrieves users; it cannot create, invite or remove members.

endpoints.purpose: Admin API: list active workspace members and guest bots
Admin API: revoke a managed user's sessions
Admin API: create a permission group
Admin API: add a group member
Admin API: change a member's role in a group
Admin API: remove a group member
Public API (api.notion.com): list workspace users, guests excluded
Public API: retrieve the token's bot user

webhooks_user_events.notes: Public API webhook event types cover pages, databases, data sources and comments only; user activity is available through the Enterprise SIEM stream.

audit_log_api.notes: Audit log is Enterprise (in-app) and can be streamed to a SIEM via webhook; no REST audit-log endpoint documented.

rate_limits.text: Per-connection limit of 600 requests/minute on Business and Enterprise and 180/minute on other plans, plus a per-workspace limit (public API).

limitations.text: Admin API user and permission-group scopes are only for eligible Enterprise organizations.
Public API cannot filter users by email or name and excludes guests from list results.

fallbacks.notes: SAML 'Automatic account creation' creates accounts for new SSO users on selected domains (Business and Enterprise).

conflicts.text: Notion's SCIM API doc uses https://api.notion.com/scim/v2, while its IdP setup guide gives the tenant URL as https://app.notion.com/scim/v2.
JumpCloud's Notion guide lists 'a Business or Enterprise plan' as a prerequisite, while Notion says SCIM is Enterprise-only (JumpCloud's line likely covers SSO). Notion's page is used.
Notion's SCIM doc names Okta, OneLogin, Rippling and custom SCIM as supported, but Notion's IdP guide also documents Azure (Entra) and Google; JumpCloud publishes its own connector.

open_questions: SCIM token expiry beyond owner-departure revocation is not documented.
Reactivation behaviour (re-adding a removed member via SCIM) is not documented beyond POST adding existing accounts.
Whether the Schemas endpoint and filtering by userName/externalId are supported is not documented.
No REST audit-log API documented; only in-app log and SIEM webhook stream.
Okta/Entra catalogue apps: who built them is not stated.
